bihar_raw_news.title: Supreme Court Allows Ayurvedic Lecturers' Appeals Against Termination of Services Due to ...
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Judgement Scroll Down To Discover Supreme Court Supreme Court Allows Ayurvedic Lecturers' Appeals Against Termination of Services Due to Misinterpretation of Eligibility Criteria. Court Found that Eligibility Should be Assessed Based on Cutoff Date, Not Initial Appointment Date Under Bihar Private Medical (Indian System of Medicine) College (Taking over) Act, 1985. Admin 2026-10-26 02:14:50 9 Share This Article: Font size: Print Case Note & Summary The case involved five appellants who were appointed as Lecturers in private Ayurvedic Colleges between March 14, 1978, and May 10, 1979, and later promoted to Reader/Professor. Following the enactment of the Bihar Private Medical (Indian System of Medicine) College (Taking over) Act, 1985, the State of Bihar took over management of private Ayurvedic colleges, including the Sri Dhanwantri Ayurved College. A Screening Committee was constituted to assess the qualifications of teaching staff, leading to the absorption of some employees while others, including the appellants, were terminated due to a lack of post-qualification teaching experience. The appellants challenged their termination in the High Court, which upheld the decision based on the requirement of three years of teaching experience as per the CCIM Act, 1970. The Supreme Court found that the High Court erred in assessing eligibility based on initial appointment dates rather than the cutoff date of June 1, 1986, as specified in the notification. The Court ruled that the appellants were eligible for absorption and ordered their reinstatement with consequential benefits, while also addressing the issue of superannuation for some appellants. The appeals were allowed, and the High Court's judgments were quashed. Headnote A) Administrative Law - Absorption of Employees - Eligibility Criteria - Bihar Private Medical (Indian System of Medicine) College (Taking over) Act, 1985, Section 3, 6 - The court held that the eligibility of teaching staff should be assessed based on qualifications and experience as of the cutoff date, not the date of initial appointment. The High Court's conclusion that the appellants lacked necessary experience was found to be a misconception of law (Paras 24-29). bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar School Labs Face November Deadline After Construction Slows - Urban Acres
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Bihar School Labs Face November Deadline After Construction Slows Breaking News Bihar School Labs Face November Deadline After Construction Slows By Tenzin Choden October 26, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Bihar education authorities have issued show-cause notices to RailTel and Telecommunications Consultants India Ltd (TCIL) after science laboratory construction was completed in only 351 of 2,199 government secondary and higher secondary schools across the state. Both agencies have been ordered to accelerate the work and meet a November 30 deadline. The action followed a review conducted on October 24 by Navdeep Shukla, state project director of the Bihar Education Project Council. According to a department communique, RailTel had completed laboratories in 78 of the 1,055 schools assigned to it, while TCIL had completed work in 273 of the 1,144 schools allotted to it. The review also found that construction had not started in some schools. The laboratories are being established under the Samagra Shiksha scheme on a turnkey basis and are intended to provide physics, chemistry and biology facilities in government schools. Under the revised directions, RailTel must complete work in 518 schools and TCIL in 816 schools by November 30. The agencies are also required to supply furniture and equipment and hand over the completed laboratories to the respective headmasters. The education department has warned that penalties could be imposed if the agencies fail to meet the targets. TCIL has been assigned work across 20 districts, while RailTel is responsible for 18 districts. The distribution of work means that the implementation delay spans multiple administrative jurisdictions rather than being limited to a single school or district. The department has directed district education officers, district programme officers and Samagra Shiksha officials to monitor progress regularly, coordinate with the executing agencies and resolve obstacles promptly. The project director also emphasised that construction quality must be maintained while the work is expedited. Engineers have been instructed to conduct field visits to check progress and ensure that the laboratories are completed to the required standard. The directions cover not only civil construction but also the delivery of furniture and laboratory equipment before the facilities are handed over. The figures in the department’s review show that 1,848 of the 2,199 planned laboratories remained incomplete at the time of assessment. RailTel had completed roughly 7% of its assigned work, while TCIL had completed roughly 24% of its allocation. The November 30 deadline therefore requires both agencies to complete the majority of their pending assignments within the period set by the state authorities. The show-cause notices place responsibility for explaining the delay on the two executing agencies. District-level officials and engineers have been given a monitoring role as the department seeks to move the project from construction to operational handover. The next formal milestone is the November 30 completion deadline, when the agencies are expected to finish the remaining laboratories, provide the required equipment and transfer the facilities to schools. national_raw_news.title: Brazil’s left-wing President Lula da Silva elected for fourth term
national_raw_news.content: In Brazil, Leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva has defeated right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro in Brazil’s intense presidential race. With this victory, Lula has become the only politician in modern Brazilian history who successfully rebound and win the second round after falling behind in the first. Incumbent Lula won the final runoff election with 51 percent of the vote and more than 51.49 million ballots. Meanwhile, Bolsonaro received 48.68 percent of the vote, which amounted to 48.8 million ballots. Just over 2.6 million votes separated the two candidates. Because of the close and highly contested race, voting stations across the country remained open two hours longer than originally planned. The former metalworker union leader, at the age of 80 will be sworn into office on 5th of January next year, breaking his own record as the oldest president to take the oath of office since Brazil returned to a democracy. This victory marks an unprecedented fourth non-consecutive term for Lula, who has run for the presidency a total of seven times. During his campaign, Lula has rallied supporters around cost-of-living issues. He championed a constitutional amendment passed this month that reduces the Brazilian workweek, and floated the possibility of providing free public transport on weekends. Lula’s victory stops a recent regional trend in South America, where right-wing leaders have swept recent presidential elections in nearby countries like Peru, Colombia, Argentina, Bolivia, and Ecuador.

national_raw_news.title: India to expand its space operations with four functional launch pads by 2029, says ISRO Chairman
national_raw_news.content: ISRO Chairman V Narayanan has said that India will expand its space operations significantly with four functional launch pads by the year 2029. Mr. Narayanan said, these include a 2000 acre dedicated Small Satellite Launch Vehicle (SSLV) complex at Kulasekarapattinam in Tuticorin district of Tamil Nadu and a third launch pad at Sriharikota, to meet the global demand for satellite launches. He was addressing convocation of a private university at Porur near Chennai. The ISRO chief said that the upcoming Kulasekarapattinam spaceport facility will feature crucial infrastructure such as integration buildings, launch pads, rail-track systems, telemetry, tracking, and command systems. Mr. Narayanan stated that ISRO plans to conduct the first uncrewed Gaganyaan test within the next two months, followed by two subsequent uncrewed tests before the crewed mission. These preliminary tests will evaluate environmental control, safety systems, crew escape mechanisms, and module interiors under varying pressure, temperature, and humidity conditions. ISRO successfully conducted approximately 8 thousand ground-based experiments for the mission, and four astronaut-designates are currently undergoing specialised training. Mr. Narayanan further revealed plans for Chandrayaan-5, a collaborative lunar mission with Japan’s space agency featuring a 350 kg rover designed to conduct 100 days of surface experiments. He also clarified that the national space agency will not be privatised. ISRO Chairman emphasised that partnering with private firms was essential to meet surging global and domestic demands for thousands of satellites.

national_raw_news.content: The Andhra Pradesh and adjoining South Odisha coasts have been placed under an Orange Alert as a Deep Depression over the East Central and Southeast Bay of Bengal rapidly intensifies into a major storm system. To counter the threat, the Andhra Pradesh state government is actively coordinating across all departments to deploy emergency resources, secure vulnerable areas, and prevent loss of life and property. According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the system is moving west-northwestward at 15 kmph and was last located roughly 730 km east-southeast of Visakhapatnam and 990 km east of Bapatla. It was strengthened into a cyclonic storm during early hours, escalate into a severe cyclonic storm by tomorrow, and peak as a very severe cyclonic storm as it nears the West Central Bay of Bengal. Landfall is expected by the forenoon of October 28, crossing the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam with destructive sustained wind speeds of 115-125 kmph, gusting up to 140 kmph. In anticipation of the cyclone’s impact, the IMD has warned of widespread heavy rainfall over the next two days and has urged the public to remain on high alert. Residents are strongly advised to postpone any travel plans, while fishermen have been strictly ordered not to venture into the sea.

national_raw_news.title: Use of terrorism as instrument of statecraft cannot be justified or rationalised, says EAM S Jais...
national_raw_news.content: External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar has said that the use of terrorism as an instrument of statecraft is simply unacceptable, and it can never be justified or rationalised. He said, terrorism continues because not all states display zero tolerance for the menace. Dr Jaishankar was addressing an event held in New Delhi to mark 75th anniversary of Chinmaya Mission. He said, the world must develop sharper awareness about this common threat, and it must come together with stronger resolve to counter terrorism in all its forms and manifestations. He underlined the importance of peace, especially amid the ongoing conflicts in the world, and cautioned that war anywhere threatens peace everywhere. Dr Jaishankar cited the two major conflicts going on in the world, in Ukraine and in West Asia, and said societies and economies and people far away who have little say in the matter are actually paying the cost. External Affairs Minister said, India expresses global sentiment when we urge that dialogue and diplomacy are the only solution. The minister underlined that India is making efforts towards peace building and is open to working with other partners to that end. Dr Jaishankar reiterated that the Global South today faces a ‘4F’ crisis — of finance, fuel, food and fertiliser and said the Global North must realise that it has “equal stakes” in finding solutions. He said, international economy must be urgently derisked and nations provided with more diversified options. Stressing the need for a genuine dialogue, the minister said, market distortions through constriction and chokepoints only add to suffering. Dr Jaishankar said, United Nations must show leadership, and not be a spectator to global crises. He asserted that the case for reformed multilateralism gets stronger by the day.

national_raw_news.title: Deep depression over Bay of Bengal likely to intensify into cyclonic storm today 2 hours ago 136
national_raw_news.content: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) has said that the Deep Depression over Bay of Bengal will intensify further into a Cyclonic Storm today. IMD has advised the fisherman not to venture into West central and adjoining Northwest and Southwest Bay of Bengal during the next two days. Talking to Akashvani News, Director General of IMD, Dr Mrutyunjay Mohapatra said, due to influence of depression the sea condition is very rough and will deteriorate further. He said that the wind speed may lead to large scale damage of structures and standing crops. He said that heavy to extremely heavy rainfall may hit parts of Andhra Pradesh, Odisha and Chhattisgarh during the next two days. Dr Mohapatra added that due to heavy rainfall can cause flooding in low-lying areas and landslides in hilly areas and urged the people living in these regions to be cautious. Meanwhile, the Weather Agency has issued an orange colour warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall over Kerala, Mahe, Tamil Nadu, Puducherry and Karaikal for today. Heavy Rainfall is also expected over Coastal Andhra Pradesh till tomorrow. Met Department has predicted thunderstorms accompanied by lightning and gusty winds over Gangetic West Bengal, Kerala, Mahe, Lakshadweep and Andaman and Nicobar Islands during the next two days.

national_raw_news.title: PM Modi Inaugurates RBI’s Data Centre, Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Sunday inaugurated the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI) newly established Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute in Bhubaneswar, Odisha, describing the facilities as an important step towards strengthening India’s digital infrastructure and safeguarding its financial system against emerging cyber threats. Invoking the blessings of Lord Jagannath, PM Modi said the inauguration marked a significant occasion for Odisha and the country. He congratulated the RBI and all those associated with establishing the two facilities. Addressing the gathering, the Prime Minister said India’s governance model was driven by the principles of pro-people, proactive and good governance, with a focus on equitable development and ensuring that opportunities reach villages and smaller towns. He highlighted the expansion of infrastructure, healthcare facilities and digital connectivity, saying that improving citizens’ lives and creating new opportunities had become central to governance. Digital Banking Expands Financial Inclusion PM Modi said India had witnessed a major transformation in financial inclusion, with digital banking connecting people across the country to round-the-clock banking services. He noted that nearly 60 crore Jan Dhan accounts had been opened, enabling the direct transfer of government benefits to beneficiaries and helping eliminate leakages in the delivery of welfare assistance. The Prime Minister also highlighted the role of the Pradhan Mantri Mudra Yojana, PM SVANidhi and PM Vishwakarma in expanding access to formal credit. He said small entrepreneurs, street vendors, traditional artisans and workers in the unorganised sector were now able to access loans without the need for conventional collateral. According to PM Modi, around 13 crore people had become first-time entrepreneurs under the Mudra Yojana. He also highlighted financial assistance extended to Self-Help Groups representing 10 crore rural women. He credited the RBI, commercial banks and banking employees for expanding access to financial services, including through the widespread adoption of RuPay cards. Social Security Schemes Strengthen Financial Protection The Prime Minister also underlined the contribution of social security schemes in extending financial protection to vulnerable sections of society. He said the Atal Pension Yojana covered around nine crore citizens, including 38 lakh beneficiaries in Odisha. PM Modi highlighted the Pradhan Mantri Suraksha Bima Yojana, which provides accident insurance, and the Pradhan Mantri Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana, which offers life insurance at affordable premiums. He said insurance coverage and timely claim payments had helped families cope with financial difficulties, describing these initiatives as an example of good governance. Cybersecurity Key to Protecting India’s Financial System Emphasising the importance of the newly inaugurated facilities, PM Modi said the focus of the past decade had been on bringing the unbanked into the formal banking system, while the coming decade would concentrate on making banking more efficient, reliable and secure. He warned that modern conflicts were no longer limited to conventional weapons, as cyberattacks could also target and weaken a country’s economy. PM Modi said protecting India’s expanding financial system from cybercriminals and cyberterrorists was essential as the country strengthened its economic position. He underscored the need for modern computing infrastructure, advanced cybersecurity capabilities and specialised training to address emerging threats. The new Data Centre and Cybersecurity Training Institute are expected to strengthen the RBI’s technological infrastructure and cybersecurity preparedness. Odisha Emerging as a Growth Hub PM Modi also highlighted the growing economic potential of eastern India, describing the region as an important driver of the vision of Viksit Bharat. He said Odisha was expanding beyond its traditional mineral-based industries and developing new opportunities in semiconductors, electronics, data centres and advanced computing. The Prime Minister expressed confidence that the emerging sectors would create fresh opportunities for the state’s youth and contribute to Odisha’s economic transformation. He concluded by extending festive greetings and invoking the slogan “Jai Jagannath”. -PIB
